rationale_bullets: ACLED data shows a 101% surge in fatalities in the trailing 3 months (489 deaths) compared to the prior 3-month period, demonstrating a significant departure from the post-2021 baseline trajectory.|Bilateral military friction along the Durand Line escalated into active cross-border hostilities between Pakistani security forces and Interim Taliban Authority forces in late September and October 2026, introducing state-on-state military operations.

NMME seasonal forecasts for leads 1-3 project near- to slightly above-normal precipitation (Lead 1: 51% chance of wet month, +0.52 mm/day anomaly), supported by a very strong El Niño state (+2.80°C ONI) which historically correlates with average or above-average winter precipitation in Central Asia.|Recent IPC food security assessments (October 2026) note that improved rainfall and better agricultural production supported food availability, confirming that current acute food security stress is driven by chronic economic collapse, refugee returns, and standard winter lean-season dynamics rather than a new drought regime departure.

NMME seasonal outlook indicates a 51% probability of upper-tercile precipitation in Lead 1 (+0.52 mm/day anomaly), accompanied by significant positive temperature anomalies (+2.26°C).|A very strong El Niño event (ONI +2.80°C, weekly +3.3°C) is established, which historically amplifies winter precipitation and temperatures across South and Central Asia.

A very strong El Niño event (Niño 3.4 weekly anomaly +3.3°C, ONI +2.80°C) combined with extreme positive temperature anomalies (+2.35°C) is significantly increasing drought severity in Andean and southern regions of Peru.|The Peruvian government has declared a State of Emergency across 607 districts specifically targeting El Niño-driven drought risk, indicating a substantial break from baseline operational conditions.

A major 'Super El Niño' event with ONI at +2.8°C and weekly Niño 3.4 reaching +3.3°C is forecast by ENFEN and NOAA to peak between December 2026 and March 2027, driving anomalous extreme precipitation.|Early Nov 2026 heavy rainfall and river overflows (e.g., Zarumilla River in Tumbes) have already triggered local emergency declarations, affected over 900 people, and led to national emergency preparations.

Sudan remains in an established high-intensity civil war baseline, with 2,841 fatalities recorded in the last 3 months, closely tracking its trailing 12-month quarterly average (~2,738 fatalities/quarter).|Although ACLED recorded a 36% fatality increase in the trailing 3 months relative to the preceding quarter, recent operational dynamics (RSF offensives in Blue Nile, SAF counter-advances in North Kordofan, and widespread drone strikes) represent shifting active fronts within an ongoing conflict stalemate rather than a regime change.

Severe El Niño-driven drought during the 2026 growing season has caused anomalous vegetation failure, affecting nearly two-thirds of cropland in North Darfur and about half in South Darfur (UN News, Al Jazeera, October 2026).|Humanitarian reports from UNICEF (November 2026) and IRC confirm that drought damage to crops cannot be undone by late rains, with large-scale producers reporting harvest yield drops of up to 75%.
